In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work demonstrates the possibility of implementing high-speed serial data links using a standard 0.8/spl mu/m CMOS technology.
this thesis presents a 2.488 Gbit/s serial data link receiver and transmitter, implemented in 0.8 μm CMOS technology, that uses multiple phased clocks for demultiplexing and multiplexing serial data.
this thesis has successfully demonstrated the feasibility of implementing a CMOS OC-48 serial data link.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed oversampled receiver and transmitter can be used to implement a serial transceiver that can operate at a data rate of up to 2.5Gb/s in a 0/spl sim/3/sup 2/ area in a standard digital CMOS process.
the 2.5-Gb/s serial data link is feasible using a 0.5-μm CM OS process, with a power consumption of 1 W and an eye opening of 1.1 V.
the use of multiple phased clocks can be an effective approach to overcome the gate speed limitations of the CMOS technology in serial link designs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oversampling approach to high speed serial links is viable and that the 3/spl x/ oversampling approach is the most practical.
a 0.5-μm CMOST process is capable of achieving the required performance for 2.5-Gb/s serial links.
oversampling can be used to overcome the gate-speed limitations of CMOS circuits and to provide a low-cost solution for OC-48 serial links.
